chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Cleaning up the band section by section
summary: McRae and Taft Jordan began rehearsals to tighten the sections; a leader assigns solos to who can play them and knows the men.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: He say, "Maybe that's what Chick needed all the time. Need somebody to give the band a lift," you know. And I tried to do that. And I had an idea of always -- perfection or something. When I joined the band, a lot of things I didn't know about Chick's band. I said - we (inaudible) started calling rehearsal, you know. And we began to clean up things. Taft began to clean up at that time -- he had charge of the brass -- and he began to clean up the brass section -- trombone and things like that. And we began to work together --
The different sections would start working --

Yeah, begin working towards the building the band. Trying to make the band better than what it was, you know. Not just going along playing all the time, you know, trying to make something better, you know. A lot of things go on in a band like a lady around the house. She's always cleaning or

fixing this or putting up new curtains and things. The same way we had to with a band.
You got to continue always doing something with it. If a new man come in, you got to take him through the work.
That might sound like a lot of work, but ain't much you got to show him. You got to show him the fundamental points what you want him to do, you know.
Like when an arranger brings an arrangement in, he writes in certain musicians for a certain solo.
Now supposed you're playing second trumpet and third trumpet, and somebody bring an arrangement in on a song, and it's got a solo in it, you know.

And you play it and you don't do nothing with it. So we take the part away from you and say, 'Look, you play this part, and let him play that solo because he can do more with it than you can,' you know. No hard feelings!

Sometimes in the band some musicians can play different things better than other musicians, you know.
So they tell arrangers, "Don't write so and so and so. Write in so and so. Don't write in" --
You got to know your musicians. Don't embarrass them by bringing in something for them to do that they can't do, you know.
